authors: Li, Y., Wang, N., Shi, J., Hou, X. & Liu, J.
title: Adaptive batch normalization for practical domain adaptation
relevance: Establishes the premise both sides of our FREEZE_ENCODER_BN argument depend on: BN statistics encode DOMAIN-SPECIFIC information, so replacing source statistics with target-domain statistics adapts the model with no labels and no retraining. This is the peer-reviewed version of the claim that our v039 freeze appears to contradict, and it is estimated over the whole target domain rather than per batch - which is exactly why it does not suffer the small-batch instability that motivated our freeze. Reframes the conflict: v039 and AdaBN disagree about WHEN statistics are estimated, not about whether BN carries domain information.

authors: Chang, W.-G., You, T., Seo, S., Kwak, S. & Han, B.
title: Domain-specific batch normalization for unsupervised domain adaptation
relevance: Resolves the conflict instead of picking a side: keep a SEPARATE BN branch per domain, so each domain gets its own statistics while all other weights stay shared. That is directly buildable for us and it composes with the iteration-11 finding - use one BN branch per RADIOMETRIC CLUSTER rather than per agency. It gives per-year statistics without the small-batch instability that motivated FREEZE_ENCODER_BN, because each branch is estimated over a whole domain offline rather than online per batch. Strongest candidate yet for replacing the per-(sensor x era) anchor idea with something the network actually implements.
